title: Linear inequalities and number-line solutions
summary: Solve linear inequalities accurately, reverse the sign when required and represent endpoints and direction on a number line.
objectives: Solve one-step and multi-step linear inequalities.
Explain when and why the inequality sign reverses.
Draw open and closed endpoints and shade the correct direction on a number line.

blocks.text: Most steps used for equations also work for inequalities: simplify both sides, collect variable terms and isolate the variable. Addition and subtraction preserve order. Multiplication or division by a positive number also preserves order.

sections.title: Reverse when multiplying or dividing by a negative

blocks.text: If 2<5, multiplying by -1 gives -2>-5. The order reverses because points reflect across zero. Therefore dividing -3x>12 by -3 produces x<-4. Write the reversed sign during the division step rather than trying to repair it later.

Use an open circle for < or > because the boundary is excluded. Use a filled circle for ≤ or ≥ because the boundary is included. Shade left for values smaller than the boundary and right for larger values. Test one shaded value in the original inequality to catch direction errors.

sections.title: Solve and draw

prompt.text: Solve 3x+2≤14 and describe its number-line graph.

content.text: Place a filled circle at 4 and shade left.

sections.verification_note: The test value x=0 gives 2≤14, so the shaded side is correct.

sections.title: Handle a negative coefficient

content.text: Divide by -2 and reverse the sign.

sections.verification_note: Testing x=-5 gives 17>15, while x=0 does not work.

prompt.text: For 2x-1<7, the solution is x<k. Find k.

feedback.text: Add 1 and divide by 2 to obtain x<4.

blocks.text: Name the mathematical relationship, choose a method that preserves it, and show each transformation clearly.
Check the result in every original condition and interpret endpoints, coordinates, roots or quantities in the form requested.
